finding: The dividend route is priced at the statutory 20% although the treaty caps Chinese tax at 10% for a U.S.-resident beneficial owner. The L09 row and the tax page therefore overstate Chinese tax by up to $40,000 at $400,000.
evidence: Treaty Art. 9(2); SAT 2019 No. 35 Arts. 3, 6, 7. The 10% applies only if the relief form is submitted and the U.S. residency certificate retained. The combined U.S. and China burden is not modelled here because the foreign tax credit would partly offset whichever rate China applies.

finding: The tax page states the FBAR willful ceiling as USD 165,353 without the statute's 50%-of-balance alternative.
evidence: 31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(5)(C)(i) gives the greater of $100,000 (inflation-adjusted to $165,353) or 50% of the balance. Above a $330,706 balance the 50% prong is larger; at $400,000 it is $200,000.

finding: The tax page describes the USD 50,000 对外支付税务备案 as applying to any single outbound payment. The announcement frames the duty for 境内机构和个人, and its Article 4 sends foreign individuals to the personal foreign-exchange rules instead.
evidence: SAT/SAFE Announcement 2013 No. 40, Arts. 1 and 4. The bank-side document requirement for a foreign individual is the separate one in Guidelines Art. 59: ID plus source-of-funds materials including tax evidence.
